A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWIRL research. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original gridworld simulations and analyses of labyrinth and spontaneous mouse behavior, including reward recovery, likelihood comparisons, segmentation and robustness results.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and animal-data analyses and adds a model-free SWIRL reward-recovery experiment in Appendix D.1.

M1.justification: v1 discusses IQ-Learn integration as future work; v2 implements it in Appendix D.1 using a posterior-weighted inverse-Q-learning objective. This adds a substantive alternative learning procedure. The original history augmentation, state-dependent switching and model-based procedure remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 5x5 gridworld, 127-node mouse labyrinth and spontaneous-behavior syllable dataset. The added model-free experiment reuses the existing gridworld without introducing another task, population or environment.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MaxEnt, I-1/Multi-intention IQL, I-2, S-1/Locally Consistent IRL and S-2, with ARHMM and rARHMM additionally evaluated on spontaneous behavior. IQ-Learn becomes part of a proposed SWIRL variant, not a separately evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The original 80/20 splits, trajectory counts and lengths, preprocessing, metrics and mode/history sweeps are retained. Appendix D.1 reuses the gridworld and reward-correlation assessment. Newly specified optimizers, iteration counts and Viterbi decoding document settings rather than establish revisions to existing protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a test of replacing Soft-Q iteration with IQ-Learn, examining whether reward recovery survives that substitution and noting noisier maps. Existing history-length, hidden-mode, discount-factor, perturbation and labyrinth case analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix B.1 specifies 20 random seeds and selection of the best 10 fits by training likelihood. v2 removes that disclosure while adding 'over 10 runs' to several captions. Standard-deviation bands and boxplot conventions remain; the PDFs do not establish an actual reduction in runs.

E6.justification: Figure 4 replaces the spontaneous-behavior reward maps and segmentations. Its five dopamine correlations change from 0.14, 0.23, 0.28, 0.22, 0.32 to 0.40, 0.04, 0.18, 0.48, 0.27, beyond relabeling modes. Appendix D.1 adds model-free reward correlation 0.737. Existing likelihood comparisons and gridworld/labyrinth findings remain stable.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix A.2's convergence argument and Appendix A.3's time/space complexity derivations. It adds the regularized IQ-Learn formulation and its posterior-weighted SWIRL objective in Appendix D.1. The original EM derivation is retained under renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central novelty and history-dependency claims. The Discussion now presents IQ-Learn integration as a demonstrated capability, extending the contribution beyond v1's proposed future reformulation.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 develops new activity, exploration and quiescence interpretations for the revised latent modes. Section 3.5 explicitly distinguishes history augmentation from formal POMDP inference. v2 also explains the small-data rationale for Soft-Q iteration and the noisier model-free recovery, while omitting v1's explicit discrete-space scalability restriction.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code link and substantially expands implementation information: Adam/BFGS/LBFGS choices, learning rate, momentum coefficients, tolerances and 100 Soft-Q iterations. New Appendix B.3-B.4 specifies metric computation, Viterbi decoding and labyrinth actions. These are newly documented details, not demonstrated changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: The main related-work positioning remains stable. v2 removes the adversarial-IRL discussion and references to Fu et al. (2018), Chen et al. (2023), and the convergence reference Wu (1983). Previously cited IQ-Learn and MaxEnt connections receive greater emphasis.

P1.justification: Rewriting concentrates on inference, spontaneous-behavior interpretation and Discussion; much of the introduction, related work and experimental narrative remains close. Algorithm 1 moves into Appendix A.1, Appendix B is reorganized, and an Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main text and extensively rearranges figure panels, notably Figures 2-3. Figure 4 changes its segmentation display, colors and legend placement; appendix figures are resized and repositioned. New Figure 9 displays model-free reward recovery.

improvement.justification: Explicit optimizer settings, metric computations and a code link improve implementability, while Appendix D.1 gives concrete support for the previously speculative IQ-Learn extension. These benefits provide a limited overall gain. Removing the complexity analysis and top-10-of-20 seed-selection disclosure weakens transparency; the revised Figure 4 correlations alone do not establish better scientific quality.
